newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber slow, buyers holding back.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber slow, buyers holding back.

text.p: Trading in the Singapore rubber market was slow at the close on Wednesday with major buyers said to be holding back on the belief that rubber prices will head lower, dealers said.
"Many of the buyers called up asking for offer prices, but I think they're just checking the level of prices and they did not call back because they feel prices will still head lower," a dealer said.
Traders said buyers have the upperhand in the market since they have ample coverage, allowing them to sit back and wait for sellers to bring down their prices.
"The buyers have the upperhand in this kind of a market. I did not see anybody in at the moment," another dealer said. One trader said some spot deals were likely done.
Traders said market activity may suffer tomorrow ahead of the Eid Al-Adha Moslem holiday on Friday, which will close markets here and in Malaysia and Indonesia.

At around 0945 GMT, June RSS3 was seen at 112.00-114.00 U.S. cents a kg from 114.00 cents. June RSS1 was seen at 160.00- 162.00 Singapore cents (US$1.11-$1.12) a kg from 163.00 cents. October/December TSR20 was seen at 112.00 U.S. cents a kg from 113.50 cents. -- (US$1-S$1.44) Rene Pastor (65-8703305)
